These two control mechanisms cover decisions in different dimensions—the former is a whitelist in the identity-and-permission dimension, the latter is a cap in the amount-and-time dimension. o4vsrx:239: AgentCore Identity presents a clear four-layer security architecture: (1) IAM/SigV4 entry authentication, (2) an AWS KMS-encrypted Token Vault storing developer credentials, (3) complete separation of wallet addresses and keys, with keys held by the wallet provider, and (4) JIT tokens used only once per payment. Each layer corresponds to a specific threat vector—layer 1 blocks unauthorized entry, layer 2 prevents developer credential leakage, layer 3 prevents end-user wallet impersonation, and layer 4 prevents token replay and session persistence. This layered design is worth adopting in any agentic system involving sensitive operations.
